{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, the passage of about 250 words that came immediately BEFORE the current text in its story.","text":"The photograph was almost lost beneath a stack of postcards, its corners softened by years of handling. Mara turned it over. Nothing was written on the back, not even a date. She held it up to the kitchen window, trying to make out the small shape beside her mother’s hand.

“Do you remember this?” she asked.

Her mother glanced over from the box she was packing. For a moment her expression changed—not quite surprise, not quite fear. Then she reached for the photograph.

“Where did you find that?”

“Under the postcards. Who’s the man in the background?”

“There’s no man.”

Mara looked again. The figure, if it was a figure, stood beyond the stone wall, blurred by the old camera. “I meant the thing by your hand.”

Her mother folded the box flaps together. “It’s a shadow.”

“Of what?”

“Your grandfather was always taking pictures in that village. He liked making everything seem mysterious.”

It was the closest her mother had come to saying Bellweather’s name all afternoon. Mara waited, but the silence settled between them again. Her mother taped the box shut and wrote Mara’s address across the top in careful block letters.

They carried the boxes to the car. At the door, Mara tried once more. “If there’s something I should know about him, I’d rather hear it from you.”

Her mother kept her eyes on the wet driveway. “There’s nothing to know.”

Mara loaded the last box into the back seat. The photograph slipped into her coat pocket. She wanted to ask another question, but her mother had already turned toward the house, one hand on the knob."}
